$comment: The Brief: one dated edition each morning. The edition itself is all sourced material and publishes directly. Prose is drafted for a handful of lead stories only and reaches the site solely through an approved pull request.
$guardNote: The model is given nothing but headlines and standfirsts already fetched from the publishers. Anything it returns containing a number absent from that material is discarded outright — a summary is allowed to compress what the sources said and nothing else.

ai.$fallbackNote: No key, empty quota, a timeout or a failed guard all end the same way: the edition publishes without prose. It must never cost money and never block the run.
ai.$modelNote: Set by measurement, not by guesswork — run npm run gemini:check after any change to the key's project tier and it will name a working model. As of the last check every Gemini model on this project reports limit: 0 (the key is valid and the API is enabled; the project simply has no allowance), and the only model that answers is a Gemma reasoning model which spends its whole output budget thinking: on a six-headline story it burned 3998 tokens in 84 seconds and produced nothing. Gemini is configured here so the step works the moment the project has quota.
ai.$tokenNote: Covers the model's own reasoning as well as the answer. Reasoning models spend this budget thinking first; too small a budget returns nothing at all rather than a short answer.
ai.$enabledNote: Off deliberately. The key's project has no Gemini allowance, so every attempt would fail and the edition would publish without prose anyway. Turning it off avoids a pointless call each morning. Set this back to true once npm run gemini:check names a working model.
